title: A snapshot of the inputs only

blocks.text: A water utility, Riverbend Water (invented for this practice), keeps its pumping plans as records like this one:

Its run service must tell whether two plans were solved on the same inputs. The inputs are the fields named in `INPUT_KEYS`: demand, budget and solver settings. Everything else (id, name, owner, creation time) is metadata and must not affect the answer.

Write `snapshot(record)` in `snapshot.py`. It returns the sha256 hex digest of the record's inputs only, written as text that is the same for the same inputs however their dictionaries were filled in. Records in the tests may carry metadata keys you have not seen. Every record carries all three input keys; one that lacks an input is malformed, and the reference lets it raise `KeyError` rather than hash an incomplete plan (no test sends one). About four lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from snapshot import snapshot

plan = {"id": "Q-3", "name": "winter", "owner": "planner-x",
        "demand": {"harbour": 25, "airport": 18}, "budget": {2030: 600, 2031: 640},
        "settings": {"solver": "HIGHS", "gap": 0.02}}
renamed = {**plan, "id": "Q-9", "name": "winter copy", "owner": "planner-y"}
reordered = {**plan, "demand": {"airport": 18, "harbour": 25}}
tighter = {**plan, "settings": {"solver": "HIGHS", "gap": 0.0}}

print("Q-3:          ", snapshot(plan))
print("renamed Q-9:  ", snapshot(renamed))
print("demand reordered:", snapshot(reordered))
print("gap 0.0:      ", snapshot(tighter))

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json

#: The fields a run is computed from. Everything else in a record is metadata.
INPUT_KEYS = ("demand", "budget", "settings")


def snapshot(record: dict) -> str:
    """sha256 hex of the record's inputs, written as canonical JSON."""
    # TODO: hash only the inputs, written so that equal inputs always give equal text.
    return hashlib.sha256(b"").hexdigest()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    plan = {"id": "W-1", "name": "base", "owner": "analyst-a",
            "demand": {"north": 41, "south": 37}, "budget": {2027: 900, 2028: 950},
            "settings": {"solver": "HIGHS", "gap": 0.0}}
    print(snapshot(plan))

cases.says: renaming a plan or changing its owner keeps its snapshot, while a budget change gives a new one
the same demand and budgets entered in another order give the same snapshot
a different gap tolerance gives a different snapshot
the snapshot is a 64-character sha256 hex digest

origin.section: The Snapshot Covers the Inputs, and Nothing About Who or When

concepts: the snapshot hashes the inputs in canonical form and ignores metadata
